The third: Ibn 'Abbas said: The Muslims asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) so many questions that they wearied him. Allah wanted to lighten the burden on His Prophet. When this verse was revealed, many people became reluctant and refrained from asking.

The fourth: Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: The wealthy overpowered the poor in the assembly of the Prophet (peace be upon him) and multiplied their private consultations with him, until the Prophet (ﷺ) disliked how long they sat. So Allah commanded charity at the time of consultation. The wealthy refrained, while the poor found nothing to give, and they longed for the assembly of the Messenger (peace be upon him). They wished that they possessed something to spend, so they could reach the assembly of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Through this obligation, the rank of the poor before Allah increased, and the rank of the wealthy was lowered.

The fifth: It may be that its purpose was to lighten the burden on him, because those with needs pressed upon the Messenger and occupied his time, which was apportioned to conveying the message to the community and to worship. It may also be that some believers' hearts were preoccupied with it, because they thought that so-and-so was consulting the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about a matter that required concern with worldly affairs.

The sixth: Through it, one who loves the Hereafter is distinguished from one who loves this world, for wealth is the touchstone of motives.

**The second issue:** The apparent meaning of the verse indicates that giving charity before consultation was obligatory, since the command denotes obligation. This is reinforced by His words at the end of the verse: ﴿But if you do not find [the means], then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. This phrase is only used for matters whose obligation lapses when the means are lacking.

Some said that it was not obligatory but recommended (mandub), and they argued with two points.

The first: He, the Exalted, said: ﴿That is better for you and purer﴾, and this expression is used for voluntary acts, not for obligatory ones.

The second: If it were obligatory, its obligation would not have been removed by a statement connected to it, namely His words: ﴿Are you apprehensive about presenting [charity] before your private conversation?﴾ up to the end of the verse.

The answer to the first: Just as the recommended act is described as better and purer, so too the obligatory act is described in the same way.

The answer to the second: It does not follow that because two verses are connected in recitation, they are connected in revelation. This is like what we say regarding the verse indicating the obligation of observing a waiting period of four months and ten days, that it abrogates the waiting period of one year, even though the abrogating verse precedes the abrogated one in recitation. Then they differed about the length of the interval between the abrogating and the abrogated ruling (naskh: abrogation). Al-Kalbi said: That obligation remained only for an hour of the day and then was abrogated. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: That obligation remained for ten days and then was abrogated.

**The third issue:** It is related from 'Ali (peace be upon him) that he said: Indeed, in the Book of Allah there is a verse that no one acted upon before me, and no one will act upon after me. I had a dinar, so I exchanged it for ten dirhams, and whenever I consulted the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), I gave one dirham before my private conversation. Then it was abrogated, and no one acted upon it.

It is also related from Ibn Jurayj, al-Kalbi and 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, that they were forbidden from private consultation until they gave charity. No one consulted him except 'Ali (peace be upon him), who gave a dinar in charity. Then the concession was revealed.

Al-Qadi and most of the narrations state that he (peace be upon him) alone gave charity before his consultation, and then the abrogation came. Although it has also been related that eminent Companions had the opportunity but did not do so. If it is established that he was singled out for this, that is because the time did not allow for this purpose. Otherwise, there is no doubt that the great Companions would not hold back from such a thing.

I say: Even if it is assumed that eminent Companions had the opportunity and did not do so, this does not bring any criticism upon them. Engaging in this action would distress the poor man, for he cannot match it, so his heart would be constricted, and it would make the wealthy man feel estranged. When the wealthy man did not do it and another did, that act became a cause for slandering those who did not do it. Thus, since this act was a cause of sorrow for the poor and estrangement for the wealthy, its abandonment does not entail great harm, because what causes harmony is preferable to what causes estrangement. Furthermore, this private consultation is neither obligatory nor a recommended act of obedience. Rather, we have explained that they were obligated to this charity only so that they would abandon this consultation. Since the better course regarding this consultation was that it be left, abandoning it did not become a cause for criticism.

**The fourth issue:** It is related from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) that he said: When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called me and said: "What do you say about a dinar?" I said: "They cannot afford it." He said: "How much?" I said: "A grain or a barleycorn." He said: "Indeed, you are frugal (zahid)." The meaning is: you have little wealth, so you assessed it according to your circumstances.

As for His words, ﴿That is better for you and purer﴾, meaning: that giving beforehand is better for you in your religion and purer, because charity is a purification.

As for His words: ﴿But if you do not find [the means], then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, what is meant by this is the poor, and this indicates that whoever does not find what he can give in charity is pardoned.

**The fifth issue:** Abu Muslim denied that abrogation occurred. He said: The hypocrites used to refrain from giving charity. Some of the hypocrites abandoned hypocrisy and believed outwardly and inwardly, with true faith. So Allah, the Exalted, wanted to distinguish them from the hypocrites. He commanded giving charity before the consultation, so that those who truly believed would be distinguished from those who remained upon their original hypocrisy. Since this obligation was for the sake of this specific benefit appropriate to that time, this obligation is naturally limited to that time.

The essence of Abu Muslim's position is that this obligation was limited by a specific endpoint, so it was required to end when that specific endpoint was reached. Therefore this is not abrogation. This argument is good and has no flaw. However, the well-known view among the majority is that it was abrogated by His words: ﴿Are you apprehensive...﴾. Some said that it was abrogated by the obligation of zakat.

**The Words of Allah, the Exalted:** ﴿Are you apprehensive that you will offer charity before your private consultation? So when you do not do it, and Allah has forgiven you, then establish prayer, give zakat, and obey Allah and His Messenger. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾

The meaning is: Are you afraid of offering charity before your consultation because it involves spending wealth? When you did not do what you were commanded, and Allah forgave you and permitted you not to do it, then do not neglect the prayer, zakat, and the rest of the acts of obedience. If it is said: the apparent meaning of the verse indicates that the believers fell short in that obligation, and this is explained in several ways:

The first is His words: ﴿Are you apprehensive that you will offer﴾, which indicates their shortcoming.

The second is His words: ﴿So when you do not do it﴾.

The third is His words: ﴿And Allah has forgiven you.﴾ We say: the matter is not as you have said. This is because when the people were obligated to offer charity before consulting the Prophet privately, offering charity was necessary. Whoever abandoned the consultation would be at fault. As for the case where it is said that they consulted him without offering charity, this too is not permissible, because private consultation is only possible if the Messenger allowed it. If he did not allow them to do so, they would not be able to consult him privately. Thus we know that the verse does not indicate that they committed a shortcoming. As for His words ﴿Are you apprehensive﴾, it is not impossible that Allah, the Exalted, knew that many of them would find it hard to give charity in the future if the obligation continued, so He said this statement. As for His words ﴿And Allah has forgiven you﴾, the verse does not say that He forgave them for this shortcoming. Rather, it is possible that when you are repentant and returning to Allah, and you establish prayer and give zakat, this obligation has been lifted from you. As for His words ﴿And Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾, it means He encompasses your deeds and your intentions.

**The Words of Allah, the Exalted:** ﴿Have you not seen those who have allied themselves with a people with whom Allah is angry? They are neither of you nor of them, and they swear falsely while they know.﴾

The hypocrites used to ally themselves with the Jews, who are the people with whom Allah became angry, as in His words: ﴿Those whom Allah has cursed and with whom He is angry﴾. They would convey the secrets of the believers to them. ﴿They are neither of you﴾, O Muslims, ﴿nor of the Jews﴾. ﴿And they swear falsely﴾. The falsehood intended here is either their claim to be Muslims, or that they used to revile Allah and His Messenger and plot against the Muslims. When they were told, "You did these things," they feared for their own lives from being killed, so they swore that "We did not say that and did not do it." This is the falsehood over which they swear.

Know that this verse refutes the view of al-Jahiz (al-Jahiz, a famous scholar of language and literature) that a report which contradicts the reality it reports is only a lie if the one reporting it knows that the report contradicts that reality. This is because, if the matter were as he claimed, His words ﴿while they know﴾ would be an unrestricted repetition.

It is narrated that Abdullah ibn Nabtal, the hypocrite, used to sit with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and then pass his words on to the Jews. Once, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was in his chamber, he said: "A man is about to enter upon you who looks with the eye of a devil" (or "with the two eyes of a devil"). Then a man entered whose eyes were blue. He said to him: "Why do you revile me?" The man began to swear. Then the words of Allah were revealed: ﴿And they swear falsely while they know﴾.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment. Indeed, evil is what they used to do.﴾ According to some of the verifiers (al-muhaqqiqun), what is meant by it is the punishment of the grave.

The second issue: His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿For them is a humiliating punishment﴾ means the punishment of the Hereafter. As for the second: it is like His saying: ﴿They swear by Allah that they are indeed among you﴾ [al-Tawbah: 56]. The meaning is that, because of their deep immersion in hypocrisy, they thought on the Day of Resurrection that they could market their lies by means of false oaths to the Knower of the unseen, so this blameworthy oath remains with them forever. **Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on Surah 58, verse 22**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers, their sons, their brothers, or their kindred. Those—He has written faith in their hearts and strengthened them with a spirit from Him, and He will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. Those are the party of Allah. Unquestionably, the party of Allah are the successful.﴾

The meaning is that faith does not combine with affection for the enemies of Allah, because whoever loves someone cannot at the same time love his enemy. This has two aspects:

The first: the two do not coexist in the heart. When love for the enemies of Allah is present in the heart, faith is not present in it, and its possessor is then a hypocrite (munafiq).

The second: the two may coexist, but it is a sin and a major transgression. In this case, the one who has this affection does not become a disbeliever because of it; rather, he is disobedient to Allah. If it is said: "The community (ummah) has agreed that it is permissible to associate with them and to live among them, so what is this forbidden and prohibited affection?" We say: The prohibited affection is the wish for their (the disbelievers') ruin in religion and in worldly matters, while they are disbelievers. As for anything other than that, there is no prohibition in it. Then He, may He be exalted, went to great lengths in forbidding this affection in several ways:

The first of them: what has been mentioned, that this affection and faith do not coexist.

The second: His saying: ﴿even if they were their fathers, their sons, their brothers, or their kindred﴾. The meaning is that the inclination toward these is the greatest kind of inclination, and despite this, this inclination must be overcome and cast aside for the sake of religion. Ibn Abbas said: "This verse was revealed concerning Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah, who killed his father Abdullah ibn al-Jarrah on the day of Uhud; and Umar ibn al-Khattab, who killed his maternal uncle al-As ibn Hisham ibn al-Mughirah on the day of Badr; and Abu Bakr, whose son invited him to single combat on the day of Badr, and the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: 'Let us benefit from you with yourself'; and Mus'ab ibn Umayr, who killed his brother Ubayd ibn Umayr; and Ali ibn Abi Talib [and Hamzah] and Ubaydah, who killed Utbah, Shaybah, and al-Walid ibn Utbah on the day of Badr." He informed that these did not show affection to their relatives and kindred out of anger for Allah and His religion.

[Page 241]

The third: He, may He be exalted, enumerated His blessings upon the believers, beginning with His saying: ﴿Those—He has written faith in their hearts﴾. Concerning this there are two issues:

The first issue: the meaning is that whoever Allah has blessed with this great favor, how could affection for the enemies of Allah arise in his heart? They differed concerning the intended meaning of His saying: ﴿has written﴾. As for al-Qadi, he mentioned three aspects in accordance with the view of the Mu'tazilah (a rationalist school that holds that man has free will and that Allah is bound to justice):

One of them: He placed in their hearts a sign by which the angels recognize the sincerity they have.

The second: it means He opened their breasts to faith through divine favors and success.

The third: it was said that "has written" means "decreed that their hearts be of this description." Know that we accept these three aspects from al-Qadi, and we derive from them the soundness of our position. For what Allah has decreed, He has known of, and He has written it in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz). If it did not come to pass, the true report of Allah would turn into a lie, and this is impossible, and what leads to an impossibility is itself impossible. Abu Ali al-Farisi said: its meaning is "gathered," and the katibah is a gathered body of an army. The implied meaning is: "Those are the ones whom Allah has gathered faith in their hearts," that is, they have been perfected and are not among those who say: ﴿We believe in some and disbelieve in others﴾ [an-Nisa: 150]. And whenever they are such, it is impossible for the affection of disbelievers to arise in their hearts. Most of our companions (the Ash'arites) said: "has written" means "established and created," because faith cannot be literally "written," so it must be interpreted as bringing into existence and creating.

The second issue: al-Mufaddal narrated from Asim: "kutiba" in the passive form, with the verb not naming its agent; the rest read "kataba" with the verb attributed to its agent.

The second blessing: His saying: ﴿and strengthened them with a spirit from Him﴾. Concerning this there are two views:

The first: Ibn Abbas said: He gave them victory over their enemy, and He called that victory a "spirit" because their affair lives through it.

The second: al-Suddi said: the pronoun in His saying ﴿from Him﴾ refers to faith, and the meaning is: He strengthened them with a spirit from faith. The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿And thus We revealed to you a spirit from Our command﴾ [ash-Shura: 52].

The third blessing: ﴿and He will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein﴾, which is an indication of the blessing of Paradise.

The fourth blessing: His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him﴾, which is the blessing of divine good pleasure (ridwan), and it is the greatest of blessings and the most exalted of ranks. Then, when He had enumerated these blessings, He mentioned the fourth of the matters that necessitate abandoning affection for the enemies of Allah, saying: ﴿Those are the party of Allah. Unquestionably, the party of Allah are the successful﴾, which stands in contrast to His saying concerning them: ﴿Those are the party of Satan. Unquestionably, the party of Satan are the losers﴾.

Know that most scholars agreed that His saying: ﴿You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger﴾ was revealed concerning Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah and his informing the people of Makkah about the march of the Prophet, peace be upon him, when he intended to conquer Makkah. That story is well known. In summary, the verse is a deterrent against showing affection toward disbelievers and sinners.

It is narrated from the Prophet, peace be upon him, that he used to say: "O Allah, do not grant to any wicked person or any sinner a favor from me, for I found in what You revealed: ﴿You will not find a people﴾ to the end of it." And Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, knows best. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and His blessings and peace be upon the chief of the messengers and the seal of the prophets, our master Muhammad, the unlettered Prophet, and upon his family and all his companions.
